title: Hair
body:
Taking the last shower of the year,
i thought of a conversation I had
this year with a hairdresser:
I sit in the familiar chair,
in front of the mirror,
she looks at me from the mirror,
he pats me on the shoulder
and tells me the epic "you're right-handed eh".
Surprised and at the same time chiseled
that he played with the odds,
i say, "Yes, but why?"
With the familiar laugh as if to say "I know"
he says to me "baldness grows on the right more than on the left".
Karaflitsa?!?!?
That's when I started talking to him about heredity,
genes,
gel I used to put on,
and other things.
He interrupted me by saying this:
"Your right hand, Giorgis,
it's your strongest.
With this you comb your hair backwards (then I had long hair).
The hairs are weaker than your hand and they surrender.
Don't forget to respect the weak.'
Caring
our weak parts,
w itness
Combing them
respecting their sensitivities •
no matter how well they hide them.
85 — m
